Desktop-Stil Raspberry Pi 5 Gehäuse (M.2 HAT+, Lüfter)

https://makerworld.com/de/models/3161278-desktop-style-raspberry-pi-5-case-m-2-hat-fan#profileId-3572718

I designed this case because I could not find an existing one that fit my setup and that I also liked the look of.

The starting constraint was airflow. The Pi 5 active cooler blows from the rear towards the front, which fixed the direction air has to travel through the case. The 40mm fan therefore works with that direction instead of against it, sitting at the lower rear as an intake.

Putting the connectors at the rear keeps the layout close to a desktop PC and makes it practical to stand next to a router. That also confirmed the airflow direction: cool air enters at the rear, warm air leaves at the front through holes hidden between the ribs of the surface pattern, so the ventilation does not interrupt the visible face of the case.

The case runs a Pi 5 with an NVMe SSD as a home server, hosting a handful of self-built web apps.

### Bill of materials

* 1x of each printed part required. For the electronics mount, choose between &#34;Electronics-Mount&#34; and &#34;Electronics-Mount_Simplified&#34;
* 1x Raspberry Pi 5 (shown with the official active cooler)
* 1x M.2 HAT+ for Raspberry Pi 5
* 1x NVMe SSD, 2230 or 2242
* 1x 4010 5V fan (shown: Noctua NF-A4x10 5V PWM)
* 1x WaveShare micro-HDMI to HDMI adapter board for Raspberry Pi 5
* 4x Magnet, 8x3 mm
* 4x M3x16 socket head cap screw
* 7x M3x10 countersunk screw
* 4x M3x16 countersunk screw
* 4x M2.5x5 pan head screw (supplied with the HAT)
* 8x M2.5x8 pan head screw (4x supplied with the HAT; 4x are optional)
* 4x M2.5x16 hex standoff (supplied with the HAT)
* 4x M2.5x3 threaded insert
* 15x M3 hex nut

### Print notes

* The version shown is multi-material and needs an AMS or equivalent. It prints fine in a single colour as well.
* Used Materials: PLA and PETG
* The parts listed as optional can be left out; the assembly is still rigid without them
* Supports: use PETG for the raft base and interface on PLA parts, and PLA on PETG parts. The two materials do not bond, so supports separate cleanly.
 

PartPause to insertBase4x M3 hex nutFront2x magnet 8x3 mmSide_left3x M3 hex nut 

### Credits

Reference models used for fit and clearance checks only, not part of this design. Full documentation, including the server setup behind it, is on GitHub.

Thanks to everyone who publishes their models for free — this one is my way of giving something back.

 

### Third-party models

* Raspberry Pi 5 with active cooler — https://grabcad.com/library/raspberry-pi-5-stock-active-cooler-1
* M.2 HAT+ for Raspberry Pi 5 — https://grabcad.com/library/waveshare-pcie-to-m-2-hat-for-pi5-1
* Noctua NF-A4x10 fan — https://grabcad.com/library/noctua-fan-nf-a4x10-flx-4010-1
* WaveShare micro-HDMI adapter board — https://grabcad.com/library/pi5-multi-connector-adapter-1

Druckeinstellungen:
- Druckprofil: Multi-color, 0.16mm layer, 2 walls, 15% infill (AMS)
- Schichthöhe: 0.16 mm
- Wandlinien: 2
- Infill: 15%
- Filament: PLA (#F7E6DE), PLA (#FFFFFF), PLA (#000000), PETG (#FFFFFF)
